title: A `Core` call whose argument is a large `string` costs time in proportion to the string's length, even when the member reads only its length.
text: Found by `tests/hostile/core/Uuid/tryParse/01-huge-broken-and-almost-valid-texts.nvs`, whose step 5 calls `Core\Uuid::tryParse` one million times on a 50,000,000-byte text and does not finish in the time limit. Measured on the pipeline `nvs`: 2,000 calls with that argument take about 1.4 s longer than 200 calls, which is about 0.7 ms a call, and `Core\Str::startsWith($huge, "x")` costs the same, so the cost is not in either member. `nvs_runtime::uuid::read` checks the length before it parses, and `Value::as_text` checks only the tag, so neither scans the text. The scan sits somewhere between the call site and the member's first line, and the stage that pays it is not located yet. A request that passes one large string to a `Core` member in a loop pays for every byte on every call, which is a latency question on the request path.
